eghrInterfaceSchematics._comment: Interface schematics for the EJAD EGHR employee portal case study. These are DIAGRAMS, not screenshots: they encode the delivered portal's layout, information architecture, RTL mirroring, light/dark surfaces and attendance state machine, without reproducing live HR records. Live captures contain employee data and are not published. The case-study page labels every one of them 'Schematic' and says so in an on-page note.
eghrInterfaceSchematics.replaceWith: scripts/capture_eghr_screenshots.py — run against a reachable EGHR instance with a demo/QA account; it writes optimised WebP next to these and repoints projects/eghr.html.

socialPreviews._comment: Open Graph / Twitter card images, composed locally from portfolio assets in the current palette. No private data.

portrait._comment: Real photograph of Mohamed Gamal. my_img.png at the repo root is the master; the served variants are resized/compressed from it and are what the pages load.

palette._comment: Every generated image is produced from the same semantic palette as the stylesheets, so a palette change regenerates the artwork rather than leaving stale colours behind.

companyLogos._comment: The supplied company marks are knockout logos — white or near-white ink on transparency. They are shown on a dark plum plate; on the previous bone plate the EJAD Digital mark was invisible. No logo is recreated or altered.

brandPolicy._comment: The portfolio is the gallery, each project is the artwork (see docs/portfolio_review_2026_10.md).
rules: No project screenshot is filtered, hue-rotated or recoloured.
No logo is recoloured. Where a logo sits on a dark plate it is because the supplied artwork is white or near-white ink; the plate is a contrast surface, not brand colour.
Generated covers use the PROJECT's own brand hue, not the portfolio palette.
Generated covers are illustrative structure, never presented as product screenshots; every figure renders as a placeholder bar so nothing reads as a reported metric.
